extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners; patent applicants, attorneys, and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on making, responding to, and formatting requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105 (what information examiners may require, when and how to require it, and how applicants must reply). Targets examiners preparing requirements and applicants responding to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat a matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Information which may be required under 37 CFR 1.105 is that information reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat a matter in a pending or abandoned application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111, in a pending or abandoned application that has entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, in a patent, or in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope extends to assignees or anyone obligated to assign an application. Authority arises from examination duties under 35 U.S.C. 131 and 132. Purpose is to improve patent quality and render better decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement must have a reasonable basis and be narrowly focused
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a reasonable basis for the information required that would aid in the examination of an application or treatment of some matter. The scope of the requirement should be narrowly defined, and a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 may only be made when the examiner has a reasonable basis for requiring information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement places a substantial burden on the applicant that is to be minimized by clearly focusing the reason for the requirement and the scope of the expected response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests seek factual information (not opinions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms 'factual' and 'facts' are included in 37 CFR 1.105 to make it clear that it is facts and factual information, that are known to applicant, or readily obtained after reasonable inquiry by applicant, that are sought, and that requirements under 37 CFR 1.105 are not requesting opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is expected to make a reasonable inquiry under the circumstances. Applicant need not derive or independently discover a fact (e.g., by experimentation) in response to a requirement. Purpose is to obtain facts known or readily obtainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information reasonably necessary for finding prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The information required would typically be that necessary for finding prior art or for resolving an issue arising from the results of the search for art or from analysis of the application file. A requirement for information necessary for finding prior art is not a substitute for the examiner performing a search of the relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must still make a search of the art according to MPEP §§ 704.01 and 904–904.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion A for requiring information for prior art (search limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s search and preliminary analysis demonstrates that the claimed subject matter cannot be adequately searched by class or keyword among patents and typical sources of non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often applies in new areas of technology without established classification or where class art diverges substantially from the claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion B for requiring information for prior art (applicant likely has info)
rubrics_metrics.description: Either the application file or the lack of relevant prior art found in the examiner’s search justifies asking the applicant if he or she has information that would be relevant to the patentability determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occurs where the application or related documents suggest the applicant likely has access to information necessary for a more complete understanding of the invention and its context (e.g., applicant-authored publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example A: Name and citation of particularly relevant indexed journal or treatise
rubrics_metrics.description: The name and citation of any particularly relevant indexed journal, or treatise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph examples may request this specifically for the relevant disclosed art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example B: Trade name of goods or services embodying claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The trade name of any goods or services the claimed subject matter is embodied in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify commercial implementations that may provide prior art or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example C: Advertising/promotional literature citations and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The citation for, the dates initially published and copies of any advertising and promotional literature prepared for any goods or services the claimed subject matter has been embodied in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful where commercial promotion may qualify as printed publication prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example D/E: Trade names/providers of competing goods/services
rubrics_metrics.description: The trade names and providers of any goods or services in competition with the goods or services the claimed subject matter has been embodied in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps define relevant product space and locate competing art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example F: Written descriptions/analyses by inventors or assignees of competing goods/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Any written descriptions or analyses, prepared by any of the inventors or assignees, of goods or services in competition with the goods or services the claimed subject matter has been embodied in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May reveal prior work, context, or related disclosures affecting patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example G: Identification of pending or abandoned applications disclosing similar subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of pending or abandoned applications filed by at least one of the inventors or assigned to the same assignee as the current application that disclose similar subject matter that are not otherwise identified in the current application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note confidentiality rules for applications filed before June 8, 1995; only required documents actually relied upon, and proper handling per MPEP §103 and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example H: Reply to a matter raised in a protest (37 CFR 1.291)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to a matter raised in a protest under 37 CFR 1.291.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require applicant response to protests that bear on examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example I: Explanation of technical material in a publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of technical material in a publication, such as one of the inventor’s publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies meaning/technical details of publications that may be prior art or relevant background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example J: Identification of changes in a reformatted continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: The identification of changes made in a reformatted continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aids examiner in locating differences and assessing new subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example K: Mark-up for a continuation-in-part showing added subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark-up for a continuation-in-part application showing the subject matter added where there is an intervening reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps determine what is new vs. previously disclosed; supports written description/novelty analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example L: Comments on a new Federal Circuit decision on point
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on a new decision by the Federal Circuit that appears on point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant input may clarify applicability of recent precedent to the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example M: Publication date of an undated document mentioned by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication date of an undated document mentioned by applicant that may qualify as printed publication prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential to determine whether the document is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102 (AIA or pre-AIA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example N: Comments on record raising derivation issues (35 U.S.C. 101/115, pre-AIA 102(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on information of record which raises a question of whether the inventor derived the invention from another under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 115, and pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where derivation or priority issues are implicated by the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example O: Art related to the claimed invention or disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Art related to the claimed invention, applicant’s disclosure, or the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General request for documents or citations that bear on the claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example P: Other factual information pertinent to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Other factual information pertinent to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for relevant facts not specifically enumerated; must still meet reasonable necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example Q/R: Clarification of means-plus-function support
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification of the correlation and identification of what structure, material, or acts set forth in the specification would be capable of carrying out a function recited in a means or steps plus function claim limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant cannot identify specification support, examiner may conclude there is no such support and make appropriate rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description/definiteness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example S: Interrogatories or stipulations of facts known to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of interrogatories or stipulations to obtain facts known to the applicant (e.g., common technical features shared among claims; support in the disclosure for means/steps-plus-function claims; portions of disclosure providing written description/enablement; meaning of claim terms; which claim portions correspond to admitted prior art; specific utility by claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatories must be factual in scope and clearly set forth; stipulations can clarify uncontroverted matters. Use form paragraphs 7.105.01 and 7.105.02 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example T: Information regarding third-party submission (37 CFR 1.290)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information from the applicant regarding a third-party submission under 37 CFR 1.290.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may request applicant information about the submission, but may not direct a requirement for information to the third party that submitted the paper (see MPEP §1134).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example U: Information regarding rescission of statement under 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78
rubrics_metrics.description: Information from the applicant regarding rescission of a statement under 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See form paragraph 7.104.02; restrict information sought to that reasonably necessary to render a decision on patentability; set two-month period for reply unless part of an Office action with SSP.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a requirement for information may be made (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 is discretionary and may be made at any time once the necessity for it is recognized. Optimum time is prior to or with a first action on the merits; ordinarily should not be made with or after a final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be made prior to first action (e.g., with a restriction requirement) when search is inadequate. With first action when file or lack of prior art justifies asking applicant. After first action rarely appropriate. Requirements normally should be non-final actions so applicant's reply can be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for appropriateness prior to first action
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors: (A) claimed subject matter in newly established art area without developed prior art pool; (B) whether applicant submitted an IDS; (C) whether specification background adequately describes background; (D) whether related documents by inventor/assignee not submitted are found; (E) whether non-patent literature is referred to but copy not supplied; (F) background describes information as known or conventional but examiner unfamiliar and can't find it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider these when deciding to issue a requirement before the first action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to a requirement must be complete and timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to requirements for information must be complete and filed within the time period set including any extensions. Failure to reply within the time period set will result in the abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All replies should be checked for completeness. Incomplete replies can be completed within the original period including extensions. Supplemental replies after expiration must comply with other rules for submissions of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56 applies to the applicant’s reply to a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, and requires that the applicant reply with information reasonably and readily available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.56's material-to-patentability threshold is substantially higher than 1.105's reasonable necessity threshold. 1.105 may require information not material to patentability; applicant not required to search for unknown information.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a complete reply to a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply is a reply to each enumerated requirement giving either the information required or a statement that the information required to be submitted is unknown and/or is not readily available to the party or parties from which it was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must make a good faith attempt and reasonable inquiry. No need to prove unavailability; a reply stating unknown or not readily available is generally sufficient unless it is clear the applicant did not understand the requirement or a more specific answer is possible. Follow-up requirement may be made where warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of an incomplete reply
rubrics_metrics.description: An incomplete reply to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement in a pending application or reexamination proceeding is handled in the same manner as an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final Office action (see 37 CFR 1.135(c) and MPEP §714.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the reply is bona fide, form paragraph 7.95 may be used to give a shortened two-month period to supply omissions. Does not apply where omission was deliberate or application is subject to a final Office action; examiner has no authority to grant an extension if the period for reply has expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for reply (statutory periods and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply, or failure to reply, to a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 will be governed by 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136. Requirements made without an action on the merits should set a shortened statutory period of two months for reply. Applicant may extend up to six months under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements sent with an Office action on the merits get the same period as the action. A 1.105 requirement is an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 for patent term adjustment purposes (see MPEP §2730).

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a requirement: benefit must exceed burden; narrowly specified
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 should be narrowly specified and limited in scope. It is a significant burden on both the applicant and the Office and is only warranted where the benefit from the information exceeds the burden in obtaining information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious to avoid over-broad requests that invite large volumes of irrelevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of the requirement (must state basis, scope, and form expected)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement must clearly indicate that a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 is being made, the basis for the requirement, and what information is being required. Requirements should specify the particular art area involved, and the particular claimed subject matter within such art area, in which the information is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement should also indicate the form the required information is expected to take (citations/copies, identification of collections, answers to questions, etc.). Generally prepare requirement as a separate document (preferable to including within an Office action). The requirement should state why it was made and how the information is necessary to examination. Interrogatories and stipulations may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed form paragraphs when preparing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.104.02; ¶ 7.105; ¶ 7.105.01; ¶ 7.105.02; ¶ 7.106–¶ 7.121; ¶ 7.122–¶ 7.126) should be used when preparing a requirement for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs include headings, specimen interrogatories/stipulations, and many tailored request templates (domain of search, level of skill, background description, products embodying invention, art suggested by applicant, lists of keywords, database citations, copies of referred art, publications authored by inventors, art relied upon for prior art description, art relied upon for development/drafting, results of prior art search, product names incorporating claimed invention/prior art, details of improvements over prior art, etc.). Use appropriate bracketed insertions and examiner notes per each form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.106 Domain of Search (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to extend the domain of search for prior art; limited amounts of art available within the Office are generally found in specified class/subclasses which describe the art; a broader range of art to search is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert description of art claimed but not found in the classification system; precede with ¶7.105 and follow with ¶7.122–¶7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.107 Level of Skill and Knowledge in the Art (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to document the level of skill and knowledge in the art of [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to support determinations of ordinary skill; follow ¶7.105 and other closing paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.108 Background Description (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to complete the background description in the disclosure by documenting [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps ensure background statements are supported by record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.109 Products and Services Embodying Invention (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to identify products and services embodying the disclosed subject matter and identify the properties of similar products and services found in the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aids in comparing claimed subject matter to real-world products.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.110 Art Suggested as Relevant (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to enter in the record the art suggested by the applicant as relevant to this examination in [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe where applicant suggests the art is relevant (specification page, paper received on date, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.111 List of Keywords (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to this requirement, please provide a list of keywords that are particularly helpful in locating publications related to the disclosed art of [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where examiner's search may be improved by applicant-provided keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.112 Citations for Electronically Searchable Databases (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a list of citations to electronically searchable databases or other indexed collections containing publications that document the knowledge within the disclosed art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps examiner identify searchable collections relevant to the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.113 Copy of Art Referred to in the Disclosure, But Not Submitted (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a copy of each of the following items of art referred to in the [1] where applicant referred to art that has not been previously submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify where in the disclosure the reference occurs (specification page or paper received on date).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.114 Copies of Publications Authored by Inventor(s) (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide copies of each publication which any of the inventors authored or co-authored and which describe the disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preceded by ¶7.105 and followed by closing form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.115 Art Relied Upon for Description of Prior Art (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the title, citation and copy of each publication that is a source used for the description of the prior art in the disclosure, and a concise explanation of that publication’s contribution to the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on, not merely believed relevant; preceded by ¶7.105 and followed by closing paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.116 Art Relied Upon for Development of Invention (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the title, citation and copy of each publication that any of the inventors relied upon to develop the disclosed subject matter, and a concise explanation of the reliance placed on that publication in developing the disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied upon; insert description of most important inventive elements in bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.117 Art Relied Upon for Drafting Claimed Subject Matter (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the title, citation and copy of each publication that was relied upon to draft the claimed subject matter and a concise explanation of the reliance placed on that publication in distinguishing the claimed subject matter from the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied upon; for means/steps-plus-function claims identify specific page/line numbers supporting claimed structure/acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.118 Results of Prior Art Search (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether any search of prior art was performed. If a search was performed, state the citation for each prior art collection searched and provide citations/copies of any art considered material to demonstrating the knowledge of a person having ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the subject matter for which art is required in the bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.119–¶7.121 Product/prior-art and improvement detail requests (form paragraph guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for names of products/services incorporating the claimed invention (¶7.119), names of products/services incorporating disclosed prior art (¶7.120), and details of improvement over the prior art (¶7.121) including specific elements providing improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to identify real-world implementations and to obtain applicant's explanation of claim-to-art improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.122 Submission of only pertinent pages where document is large
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding with copies of documents that are bound texts or single articles over 50 pages, requirement may be met by providing copies of those pages that provide the particular subject matter indicated, or where such subject matter is not indicated, the subject matter found in applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where scope of requirement specifically includes copies of publications to avoid burden of submitting entire large documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶7.123 Waiver of fee and statement requirements for certain submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee and certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 are waived for those documents submitted in reply to this requirement, limited to documents within the scope of the requirement that are included in the applicant’s first complete communication responding to this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any supplemental replies subsequent to the first communication and any information disclosures beyond the scope of the requirement are subject to fee and certification requirements under 37 CFR 1.97 where appropriate.
